provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Licensed in some states, moderate ticket; copy leans on prep, colour help and painting an occupied home. Lead-safe credentials stay as bracketed placeholders. No paint brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Moving and covering furniture, drop cloths on floors, filling nail holes and dents, caulking trim gaps, sanding between coats, and how each room is left at the end of the day
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners judge interior painters on mess and care, not on the colour. Showing the prep is what makes a higher number feel safe.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Sample swatches painted on the wall, whole-house palettes, undertones under morning and evening light, ceiling whites, and which sheen goes in which room
pageStructurePlus.why: Colour paralysis is the main reason interior painting gets postponed. Offering help choosing turns a someday job into a booked one.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Vaulted ceilings and two-storey foyers, staircase walls, enamel on trim and interior doors, crown moulding, and the scaffolding or plank setups for high walls
pageStructurePlus.why: The hard-to-reach work is what homeowners can't do themselves, and it's where the painter's skill and equipment are easiest to see.

pageStructurePlus.contains: One floor or a few rooms at a time, kids' rooms and nurseries, pets, low-odour paint options, quiet hours for people working from home, and keeping a bathroom usable
pageStructurePlus.why: Most interior painting happens in occupied homes. A clear plan for living through it is what gets busy families to say yes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Older homes, plaster and lead-safe work
pageStructurePlus.contains: Older homes that may have lead paint, lead-safe work practices and [lead-safe certification, if held], plaster crack repair, wallpaper removal and skim coating
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners of older homes worry about lead and crumbling plaster. A page that addresses it attracts the bigger, better-paying older-home jobs.

designDirections.name: Fresh Coat
designDirections.bestFor: Small painting crews winning room-by-room jobs on a quick estimate and a phone that gets answered
designDirections.headlineSample: Interior painting in {City}, clean lines and no mess
designDirections.whyItFits: A warm cream ground and citrus accent feel like a freshly painted room, and the geometric caps keep the estimate button loud on a phone.

designDirections.name: Room Colour
designDirections.bestFor: Painting companies with finished rooms to show by colour, sheen and room type
designDirections.headlineSample: Rooms repainted with care, start to clean-up, in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Driftwood keeps the warm neutral ground and refined serif with a walnut accent that passes, so wall colours read true.

designDirections.name: Colour Studio
designDirections.bestFor: Painters doing designer colour work, plaster finishes and whole-house repaints in older homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Designer colour and fine interior painting for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Rosewood and a Didone display feel like a colour boutique, which suits painters who sell taste and finish quality rather than a room rate.

openers.line: Your painting company shows up on Maps for {City}, but there's no website behind the listing. A homeowner comparing interior painters can't see a single finished room or your prep.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what an interior painting buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing sends people to a Facebook page. Someone repainting four bedrooms and a stairwell wants to see clean ceiling lines and an estimate form, not last month's posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest room they posted.
openers.linkLine: A painting page built for the person repainting their house: {demo-link}

openers.line: The painting site on your listing still carries a free-builder banner and lists a phone number that doesn't match Maps. Small things like that send people to the next interior painter.
openers.hook: Open the site and compare its details with the listing. Note any mismatch or banner.
openers.linkLine: Your painting company, current and consistent: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your site's menu covers the whole screen and won't close. People looking for painters are usually standing in the room they want repainted.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same painting company, fixed for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask you for a painting estimate except calling. Lots of people would rather list the rooms, ceiling heights and colours they're thinking about.
openers.hook: Check for any form on the listing, social pages or site. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: An estimate form that asks for rooms, ceilings and colour ideas: {demo-link}

openers.line: That deep green dining room and the two-storey foyer you posted are proper interior painting work. They'd sell far better grouped by room than mixed in with crew photos.
openers.hook: Pick two finished rooms on their page you can name by colour or room. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your painted rooms, sorted by room and colour: {demo-link}

openers.line: Reviewers mention painters who covered every floor and left no drips on the trim. That's the reassurance a nervous homeowner wants, and it's stuck on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about cleanliness, care or timing. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews right next to the painted rooms: {demo-link}

openers.line: When it's too cold for exterior jobs, interior painting is what keeps crews busy. The painters homeowners can find in November are the ones with a full January.
openers.hook: Use this October to December. Mention their winter schedule in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A painting site ready for the winter interior season: {demo-link}

openers.line: People decide to repaint the living room on a Saturday afternoon. If the only option is a voicemail, they've messaged three other painters by Monday.
openers.hook: Call their listed number on a weekend. If it's voicemail only and there's no form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A painting estimate request that works on weekends: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring painters. Experienced brush-and-roll people look up a painting company before they apply, the same way customers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A painting site with a careers page for painters: {demo-link}

openers.line: You paint interiors across {City}, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} that you work there. 'Interior painters' plus their town is what they search.
openers.hook: Find towns in their reviews or posts. Use the one furthest from their base.
openers.linkLine: An interior painting page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Plenty of interior painting jobs stall on colour. If you help people choose, that belongs on the site, because it's the reason they'd pick you.
openers.hook: Look for any post about colour samples or consultations. If they offer it, lead with it.
openers.linkLine: A colour consultation page for your painting company: {demo-link}

openers.line: Letting a painting crew into your home means trusting them with your floors and furniture. A page showing your licence and insurance answers the first worry before the estimate.
openers.hook: Check the state registry if painting needs a licence there. Note that a record exists; never quote a number.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and prep standards on one painting page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your painting work comes from past customers. Even a referred homeowner searches your name before letting a crew in, and right now they find a listing with no site.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'friends recommended' or 'used them twice'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a painting referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted has crisp cut lines at the ceiling. A painted room like that should be the first thing a stranger sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished room and name it exactly: colour and room.
openers.linkLine: That painted room, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted has really clean cut lines.

I was searching interior painters in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site where someone can see finished rooms or ask for an estimate. I made a sample painting site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, checking back in case my message slipped by. Here's the sample interior painting site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has rooms sorted by colour, a page on how you protect floors and furniture, and an estimate form that asks for rooms and ceiling heights. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for painting companies here in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample interior painting site for {Business Name}, with finished rooms sorted by colour, a prep page and an estimate form, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you make of it?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many room and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a painting company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, about one bedroom and hallway."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and the deposit invoice. We start when it clears, and you'll have it before the winter interior season."

objections.objection: Painting is all word of mouth.
objections.handler: "It is, and that's why the site matters. The person your customer recommends you to still searches your name before letting a crew into the house."

objections.objection: People just hire the cheapest painter.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones who had paint on the hardwood last time. Showing your prep and clean-up is what makes your number make sense."

objections.objection: I mostly do exteriors, interiors are filler.
objections.handler: "Then interiors are what keep the crew paid in winter. A site that ranks for interior painting fills the cold months before they arrive."

objections.objection: I already pay for painting leads.
objections.handler: "Those go to several painters at once and you pay either way. Your own site sends that homeowner to one painting company, you."

objections.objection: My nephew can build a site.
objections.handler: "Great. Happy to share the prep page and estimate form so he can borrow them. If it stalls before winter, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: a room gallery, a prep page and an estimate form. Roughly one bedroom repaint."

email.subject: Interior painting site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for painting companies in {City}, and I made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll email the link, look whenever you're off the ladder. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} painting demo down on Friday.

Want it left up? A one-word reply is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the cold months are coming and interior painting is about to be the only work in town. Thought of you.

The painting site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a bedroom-and-hallway repaint, never to an hourly rate. Painters price by room and by day.
Price the gallery by finished rooms sorted by colour and room type, not by page count.
An estimate form that asks for rooms, ceiling heights, trim and colour ideas is worth more than a contact form. Quote it on its own.
Only quote a colour consultation page for painters who actually offer colour help.
Older-home and lead-safe pages are only for painters who hold the right credential; leave a bracketed placeholder until they supply it.
Time the launch for autumn. The site should be live before exterior work dries up.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a dozen finished rooms with colour and sheen notes.

lineItems.item: Estimate form with rooms, ceilings and colours
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, a ceiling-height field, trim and door counts and routing to two estimators.
Max with a paid consult booking, palette examples and a sample-swatch policy.
Max with step photos from their own jobs and a printable prep checklist for the homeowner.
Max with plaster repair and wallpaper removal sections and their lead-safe process written out.
Max when each page has its own finished rooms and a local review.

whatElseYouSell.name: Painted-room photo morning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Freshly painted walls look flat in phone photos. One morning with proper light across three finished rooms shows true colour and crisp lines."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, at a job with a bold wall colour.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google listing posts for painted rooms
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A new painted room on your Google listing every week, captioned with the colour and the town, so the map shows you're busy."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review request after the final walkthrough with tape
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Once the blue-tape touch-up walk is done, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while the rooms still smell like fresh paint."

whatElseYouSell.name: Winter interior painting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A November push for winter interior painting, with a slow-season slot offer, fills January and February before they go empty."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in September, run in November.

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard sign and van lettering for painting jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A painting van parked out front for three days is an ad. Lettering and a yard sign with the site make the neighbours call."

whatElseYouSell.name: Colour of the season email to past painting clients
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short seasonal email with a finished room in a new colour reminds past clients that the bedroom they didn't paint is still waiting."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there's a list of past painting customers.

whatElseYouSell.name: Realtor move-in repaint flyer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "New owners repaint before they move in. A flyer agents hand over at closing puts your painting crew in the empty house first."

withoutAI.route: Drywall finishers who patch before the paint
withoutAI.whoPays: The drywall finisher, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a wall has a fist-sized hole, you hand it to a drywall finisher before painting. That finisher probably has no site either, and you're the person to introduce us."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Drywall and paint are consecutive on almost every interior job. One introduction is a warm door.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The paint store hears 'can you recommend a painter?' all day. A find-a-painter page on their site keeps pros and homeowners coming back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Independent stores live on pro accounts, and routing homeowners to those pros keeps them loyal.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The colour consultant who sends you whole-house repaints needs a portfolio site, and your painted rooms are the proof in it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers buy websites on looks, and the painter's finished rooms are shared proof.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every apartment turnover needs fresh paint. A turnover request page for the manager routes those units to one painting company."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers want predictable turnovers and pay for tools that cut phone calls.

withoutAI.whoPays: The mover or organiser, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Movers know which houses are empty between closing and move-in, the best time to paint. They need sites, and their customers need a painter."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Empty-house painting is the easiest work there is, and movers hear about it first.

withoutAI.route: Flooring installers finishing the same rooms
withoutAI.whoPays: The flooring installer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "New floors usually mean new paint, and the order matters. The flooring installer you coordinate with needs a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Paint and floors share the same room refresh, and both trades refer constantly.

withAI.route: Wall-colour visualiser for the paint store
withAI.pitchLine: "A living-room snapshot becomes a preview with the store's own wall colours on it, so customers walk in already down to two sample pots."
withAI.whyItWorks: It brings shoppers in with a shortlist and keeps colour sales local.

withAI.route: Turnover paint scope drafter for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Move-out photos go in, and a draft paint scope by room with patch notes comes out, ready to send to one painter."
withAI.whyItWorks: Turnover speed is the manager's money, so a tool that drafts scopes gets used weekly.

withAI.pitchLine: "The drywall finisher who patches before you paint loses jobs to slow follow-up. Same follow-up setup you have, built for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: A second build of a working tool, introduced by a client who trusts you.

withAI.pitchLine: "The consultant describes the house and light, and it drafts a whole-house palette with sheens per room to edit and send."
withAI.whyItWorks: Palette documents eat consultant evenings. A drafting tool is an easy monthly line.

withAI.pitchLine: "Customers booking a move get asked if they want painting, cleaning or flooring done first, and the assistant books the trade."
withAI.whyItWorks: Movers earn referral goodwill and the painter gets empty-house jobs.

withAI.pitchLine: "The planner works out whether paint or floors go first in each room and texts both crews the plan."
withAI.whyItWorks: Bad sequencing means scuffed walls or paint on new floors. Both trades want it solved.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for painting estimates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Roller in hand and can't answer? The caller gets a text asking which rooms, the ceiling height and when they'd like the painters in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Room-by-room interior painting estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick bedrooms, living areas, ceilings and trim, and see a painting range before booking the walkthrough."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their room prices by size, ceiling and trim add-ons and minimum job.

softwareAI.name: Review replies that mention the painted room
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review gets a drafted reply in your voice naming the room and colour, ready to approve between coats."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and final-walk invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Painting deposit at booking and the balance after the touch-up walk, both sent automatically with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Room-photo wall colour preview
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads their bedroom and sees the walls in three colours before the painting estimate visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their go-to colours and finished rooms to check previews against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Walkthrough quote builder with room measures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tap through each room, wall height, doors, trim and patching, and the painting quote prints before you leave the house."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their quote template and production rates.

softwareAI.name: Weekend painting estimate line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers weekend and evening calls, asks rooms, ceilings and timing, and books the painting walkthrough."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar and the questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew schedule by house and room
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every painting job on one board with which rooms on which days, so the homeowner knows when the bedroom is out of use."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the form is producing. Needs their crews and typical rooms per day.

softwareAI.name: Paint colour record for every client
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every wall colour, sheen and room saved per house, so touch-ups and the next repaint match without guesswork."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their job notes and a habit of logging colours at the end of each job.

softwareAI.name: Wall area and paint quantity from room photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload room photos with one measurement and it drafts wall area and gallons for each colour, for you to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs past jobs with measured areas to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Room prep reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The day before the painters arrive, the homeowner gets a text: clear the shelves, take pictures off the walls, put the dog somewhere quiet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their prep checklist and booking flow.

softwareAI.name: Client page with colours and room schedule
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner confirms colours per room and sees which rooms get painted which day, so nobody's surprised at breakfast."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the crew schedule first.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on prep, colours and paint smell
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can we sleep in the room the same night' and 'do you move furniture' at midnight, from your own interior painting rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ and lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Repaint reminder for past clients
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A few years after the hallway and kids' rooms were painted, past clients get a note offering a refresh. Repeat painting from people who already trust you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with dates and rooms.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by room type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether bedrooms, stairwells or whole-house repaints actually pay best once paint, sundries and painter days are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs paint receipts and hours for a season.

softwareAI.name: Room and colour page writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Monthly drafts of interior painting pages like 'painting a two-storey foyer', written from your job notes, approved by you first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Paint store price sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When your paint store's contractor prices change, the painting estimator and quote template update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the estimator. Needs the store's price sheet.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-quote from the painting walkthrough
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house saying room, walls, ceilings, trim, and it drafts the painting quote before you're back in the van."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Turnover painting tracker for landlord accounts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every rental unit you paint for a landlord logged with its colours and dates, so the next turnover is a quick repeat."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for painters with property manager work. Needs their landlord list.

softwareAI.name: Painter applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Painter applicants answer whether they cut in freehand, run a sprayer and have a ride, so you only call real brush hands."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the room estimator for painting companies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The room-by-room painting estimator I built for one company solves a problem every residential painter has every day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Painters are numerous and their pricing logic is similar, so one tool spreads easily.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Find-a-painter locator for a paint store chain
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The regional paint store chain, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners at the colour counter ask for painters. A locator listing the chain's pro accounts keeps both sides buying there."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Paint chains compete for pro loyalty, and routing homeowners to pros earns it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member painting companies a site template with a prep page and a room estimate form as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need visible benefits. One deal reaches many painting firms.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies get painting clients all the time. License my interior painting template with the room gallery and estimate form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell the finished painting module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each painting franchisee wants their own finished rooms and reviews on the page. One template, filled per owner, with estimates routed by town."
"Every unit in the portfolio gets one turnover painting request with standard colours and a fixed window."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Big operators buy once and roll out everywhere, and paint is their most frequent turnover cost.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Brokerages give buyers a move-in services page at closing. Painting leads it, with one company per area."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agents like closing gifts that cost them little and help buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New-home owners file nail-pop and touch-up requests in their first year. A portal routes those interior painting fixes to one painter."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders hate warranty paperwork. A portal that handles it is worth paying for.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Interior paint cost sheet for painters
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Painters send in their paint and sundries receipts, and each month they see where interior paint costs are heading in their area."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built only from contributed receipts, so it never claims more than the receipts show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Painters starting their own company, per pack
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A painter leaving a crew needs a quote sheet, a prep checklist and a simple painting site. Sell the pack your first client runs on."

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A painting client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "{City} has its interior painter. The room-gallery template and the winter-season pitch go to a painting company in the next metro."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The painting company with a dead site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Painting sites with an empty gallery and a broken form are everywhere. I relaunch them on a template that already works."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already decided to buy once.

upsellLadder.offer: Painting site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Painting site and care plan on one contract, so a new room in the gallery is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review request and Google listing posts
upsellLadder.trigger: The first interior job finished since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That dining room you just painted belongs on your Google listing with a review under it."

upsellLadder.trigger: They paint a room in a bold colour they're proud of.
upsellLadder.line: "That dark green study deserves real photos. Phone shots make painted walls look flat."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of form data shows most requests are a few bedrooms asking the price first.
upsellLadder.line: "Most painting requests are two or three bedrooms and a price question. The estimator answers it first."

upsellLadder.trigger: The exterior schedule starts thinning in autumn.
upsellLadder.line: "Exterior painting is winding down. Let's fill January with interiors now."

upsellLadder.offer: Crew schedule by house and room
upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second painting crew.
upsellLadder.line: "Two crews in two houses need one board for which rooms get painted which day."

upsellLadder.trigger: A year of painting jobs since launch, with rooms and dates logged.
upsellLadder.line: "Last year's clients have rooms you didn't paint. A reminder brings the rest of the house in."
